newsitem.title: USA: Livingston Survey - US GDP +2.4 pct in 2nd half 97.
newsitem.headline: Livingston Survey - US GDP +2.4 pct in 2nd half 97.

text.p: The U.S. economy is expected to slow from a sizzling 5.8 pct growth pace in the first quarter to a more moderate 2.4 percent expansion rate in the second half of 1997, the Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia semi-annual Livingston survey of private forecasters said.
The survey also showed economists expect the nation's Gross Domestic Product (GDP) to grow by 2.2 percent in the first half of 1998.
Unemployment rate is expected to remain low. The jobless rate is seen at 5.0 percent by late 1997 and at 5.1 percent in June 1998, the survey detected.

The survey also indicated economists expect inflation to rise slightly. The nation's consumer price index (CPI) was seen rising by 2.7 percent in the second half of 1997 and jumping 3.1 percent in first half of 1998.
Housing starts are forecast to drop 6.5 percent in the second half of 1997, while retail sales are expected to grow by an annual 5.0 percent rate over the next six months.
Here follows summary of the survey:
Real GDP 2.3 pct 2.4 pct 2.2 pct 2.4 pct
Unemployment Rate 4.9 pct 5.0 pct 5.1 pct N/A
